h2: Pool Equipment Kuta & Legian – Pumps, Filters & Salt Systems
intro: If your villa or guesthouse sits along Jl. Padma or deeper into Tuban, the pool gear has probably endured years of salt-laden air, monsoon backflow and hard water. We install and repair pumps, sand and cartridge filters, chlorinators, lights and auto-fill units as part of our Pool Equipment Kuta & Legian service. Send photos on WhatsApp and we'll point you to the right fix before it becomes a full rebuild.

sections.h3: Why Salt Air and Old Lanes Wear Pools Down Faster
sections.text: Kuta and Legian sit right at the edge of the Indian Ocean, so every brass fitting, impeller shaft and chlorinator cell takes a salt-air hit that inland pools never see. Add decades-old plumbing beneath guesthouses on Jl. Padma and low-lying lanes in Tuban that flood during heavy rain, and you get pump housings full of silt, corroded multiport valves and lights that flicker then die. That combination shows up in most of our calls.

sections.h3: The Jobs That Come Up Most Often Here
sections.text: Across Legian and Kuta Beach properties the recurring tickets are a pump that won't prime or starts growling under load, filter sand turned to powder after a couple of seasons, a multiport valve handle sticking mid-cycle, salt chlorinator cells caked with calcium, and underwater lights buzzing before going dark. Guesthouses with eight or twelve rooms push their small pools harder than a single villa ever would, so wear arrives faster.

sections.h3: What to Send on WhatsApp for an Accurate Quote
sections.text: Before we quote, send a few clear photos: the pump nameplate, the filter tank top and bottom, any error codes on the chlorinator display, plus a short video of the noise if it's a sound issue. Tell us whether the pool is in a private villa or a multi-room guesthouse, roughly how old the equipment looks, and what changed just before the problem started. Cost depends entirely on the job – once we see the photos we'll give you a straight figure.

sections.h3: Keeping Your Pool Running Through Bali's Seasons
sections.text: A simple routine saves most Kuta-area pools from repeat breakdowns. Backwash the sand filter every two to three weeks, rinse it after any monsoon week when drains back up and silt enters the return lines, and wipe down metal fittings near Kuta Beach at least monthly to slow corrosion. Check that the auto-fill float isn't stuck after a flooding event, and if your chlorinator cell hasn't been cleaned in over six months, schedule it before calcium build-up forces a full replacement.

faq.q: How do I know my filter sand needs replacing?
faq.a: If fine grit is showing up in your return jets, pressure is creeping up despite regular backwashing, or the water stays cloudy no matter how long you run the pump, the granules have likely reached end-of-life and need swapping.

faq.q: Can you fix a noisy pump without replacing the whole unit?
faq.a: Often yes – bearing wear, a dry impeller seal or a misaligned shaft can all cause grinding. Send a short video on WhatsApp and we'll tell you whether a part swap will sort it or if the housing itself needs going.

faq.q: Do you work with guesthouses and small hotels as well as private villas?
faq.a: Yes. Multi-room properties along Jl. Padma and Tuban are a big part of our workload; we handle everything from a single stuck multiport valve to full equipment swaps across several pools on one site.
